rules.title: Double the last consonant: stop → stopped
rules.short_explanation: If a word ends in one vowel + one consonant and the last syllable is stressed, double the consonant before -ed, -ing, -er or -est. For example: stop → stopped, begin → beginning.
rules.tts_text: Short stressed vowel plus one consonant: double the consonant before a suffix.
rules.mnemonic: One vowel, one consonant, stressed end: double it, friend.

examples.text: The bus stopped outside the station.
She is planning a trip to Spain.
The company is beginning a new project.
examples.note: Stress on last syllable: begin → beginning.

examples.text: He admitted his mistake to the manager.
The chef chopped onions for the soup.
They are shopping for fresh vegetables.
My brother is getting a new laptop.
The student referred to her notes.
The waiter dropped a plate in the kitchen.
This hotel is bigger than the old one.
She regretted missing the last train.
The taxi stoped at the hotel.
examples.correction: The taxi stopped at the hotel.

examples.correction: I am running late for work.

examples.correction: She planned her holiday in July.

examples.correction: He admitted he was late for class.

examples.correction: The rabbit hopped across the garden.
examples.note: Double the p; hoped is another word.

examples.text: She is geting a new passport.
examples.correction: She is getting a new passport.

rules.title: Don't double: visit → visited, open → opened
rules.short_explanation: Do not double the final consonant if the last syllable is not stressed, or if the word ends in two consonants or two vowels. For example: visit → visited, open → opened, wait → waiting.
rules.tts_text: If the last syllable is not stressed, do not double the consonant.

examples.text: She visited her grandparents last summer.
examples.note: Stress is on VIS, so no doubling.

examples.text: The shop opened at eight o'clock.
examples.note: Stress is on O, so no doubling.

examples.text: We are listening to a podcast.
The waiter offered us a free dessert.
examples.note: Stress is on OF, so no doubling.

examples.text: He is entering the contest tomorrow.
They finished the project before Friday.
My cousin worked at a bakery.
examples.note: Word ends in two consonants: rk.

examples.text: The guide waited for us outside.
examples.note: Two vowels before t: no doubling.

examples.text: She is learning Slovak at university.
We developed a new filing system.
Tom is repairing his bike in the garage.
examples.note: Two vowels before r: no doubling.

examples.text: We visitted the castle in May.
examples.correction: We visited the castle in May.
examples.note: Unstressed ending: do not double t.

examples.text: The bank openned at nine.
examples.correction: The bank opened at nine.
examples.note: Unstressed ending: do not double n.

examples.text: She is listenning to music.
examples.correction: She is listening to music.
examples.note: Unstressed ending: do not double n.

examples.text: He offerred me a good job.
examples.correction: He offered me a good job.
examples.note: Stress is on OF: do not double r.

examples.text: They are enterring the building.
examples.correction: They are entering the building.
examples.note: Unstressed ending: do not double r.

examples.text: I workked in a hotel last year.
examples.correction: I worked in a hotel last year.
examples.note: Ends in two consonants: no doubling.

examples.text: The train is waitting at platform two.
examples.correction: The train is waiting at platform two.
examples.note: Two vowels before t: no doubling.

examples.text: We developped a small app together.
examples.correction: We developed a small app together.
examples.note: Stress is not on the last syllable.

examples.text: She helpped her mother cook dinner.
examples.correction: She helped her mother cook dinner.

examples.text: The soup is cookking on the stove.
examples.correction: The soup is cooking on the stove.
examples.note: Two vowels before k: no doubling.

examples.text: He repairred the old printer.
examples.correction: He repaired the old printer.
examples.note: Two vowels before r: no doubling.

examples.text: The report was submitted on Monday.
